title: High volume phishing campaign uses Microsoft 365 outage lures to target multiple industry sectors
description: A high-volume phishing campaign observed on November 13, 2026, impersonated Microsoft 365 service-health notifications to lure recipients into clicking malicious links. The emails falsely claimed that messages were held during a service outage and would be deleted within 24 hours unless restored, creating urgency to prompt user interaction. The campaign used multiple sender domains, randomized subject lines, and recipient-specific tracking URLs leading to a non-Microsoft destination. Microsoft assessed the campaign as likely credential phishing but found no direct evidence of credential capture, malware delivery, or post-compromise activity. Microsoft Defender for Office 365 currently blocks and quarantines these phishing emails.
